name: SQL (SQLite)
summary: Learn SQL queries, joins, grouping, transactions, and indexes with local SQLite.

lessons.title: Tables, constraints, and inserts
lessons.explanation: A table gives columns names and type affinities. Define keys and constraints to protect invariants. Examples in this pack can run separately in a new in-memory SQLite database.

api.name: CREATE TABLE
api.description: Declare a table and its columns.

api.name: PRIMARY KEY
api.description: Identify a row uniquely.

api.name: INSERT INTO ... VALUES
api.description: Add one or more rows.

api.name: CHECK (...)
api.description: Reject values that violate a column or row condition.

lessons.practice: Add a third topic. Try inserting negative minutes and a duplicate title.
lessons.pitfall: Column affinity is different from strict type enforcement in an ordinary SQLite table.

lessons.title: Filtering, sorting, and missing values
lessons.explanation: SELECT chooses output expressions. WHERE filters rows, and ORDER BY specifies output order. NULL represents an absent value and has its own predicates.
lessons.example:
WITH scores(name, points) AS (
    VALUES ('Ari', 8), ('Bea', NULL), ('Casey', 9), ('Dev', 4)
)
SELECT name, COALESCE(points, 0) AS shown_points
FROM scores
WHERE points >= 8 OR points IS NULL
ORDER BY shown_points DESC, name
LIMIT 3;

api.name: WHERE condition
api.description: Keep rows for which the condition is true.

api.name: IS NULL / IS NOT NULL
api.description: Test for an absent or present value.

api.name: COALESCE(a, b)
api.description: Return the first non-NULL value.

api.name: ORDER BY ... LIMIT ...
api.description: Sort results and cap the number returned.

lessons.practice: Show only rows with a real score. Sort them by points, then name.
lessons.pitfall: Use IS NULL for missing values. The expression points = NULL does not evaluate to true.

lessons.title: Relationships and joins
lessons.explanation: Join tables by matching related keys. An inner join includes only matching pairs. A left join also keeps rows from its left input that have no match and fills the right columns with NULL.
lessons.example:
WITH
  topic(id, title) AS (VALUES (1, 'Arrays'), (2, 'Loops')),
  attempt(topic_id, score) AS (VALUES (1, 8), (1, 10))
SELECT topic.title, attempt.score
FROM topic
LEFT JOIN attempt ON attempt.topic_id = topic.id
ORDER BY topic.id, attempt.score;

api.name: JOIN ... ON ...
api.description: Combine matching rows from two inputs.

api.name: LEFT JOIN ... ON ...
api.description: Keep unmatched left rows as well as matches.

api.name: REFERENCES parent(id)
api.description: Declare a foreign-key relationship. Enable PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON on each SQLite connection.

lessons.practice: Add an attempt for Loops and observe how the unmatched row changes.
lessons.pitfall: A WHERE filter on a right-table field can remove the NULL rows that a left join preserved.

lessons.title: Grouping, aggregates, and HAVING
lessons.explanation: An aggregate combines a group of rows into a result. WHERE filters individual rows before grouping. HAVING filters the groups produced by GROUP BY.
lessons.example:
WITH attempt(topic, points) AS (
    VALUES ('Arrays', 8), ('Arrays', 10), ('Loops', 6), ('Loops', NULL)
)
SELECT topic, COUNT(points) AS graded, AVG(points) AS average
FROM attempt
GROUP BY topic
HAVING AVG(points) >= 8
ORDER BY average DESC;

api.name: COUNT(*)
api.description: Count every row in the group.

api.name: COUNT(column)
api.description: Count non-NULL values in that column.

api.name: SUM() / AVG()
api.description: Calculate a sum or average over non-NULL inputs.

api.name: HAVING condition
api.description: Filter grouped results.

lessons.practice: Display total attempts and graded attempts side by side, including the group with a missing score.
lessons.pitfall: Averages are computed from non-NULL values. Treating a missing value as zero changes the result.

lessons.title: Updates, transactions, and parameters
lessons.explanation: Use transactions to group writes so they commit together. ROLLBACK discards changes from the current transaction. Application code should bind input values through parameters.

api.name: UPDATE ... SET ... WHERE ...
api.description: Change fields in selected rows.

api.name: DELETE FROM ... WHERE ...
api.description: Remove selected rows.

api.name: BEGIN / COMMIT / ROLLBACK
api.description: Start, save, or abandon a transaction.

api.name: WHERE id = ?
api.description: Use a parameter placeholder and bind it through your SQLite client.

lessons.practice: Replace COMMIT with ROLLBACK. Compare the final scores.
lessons.pitfall: An UPDATE or DELETE without WHERE targets every row. Preview the predicate with SELECT first.

lessons.title: Indexes and query plans
lessons.explanation: An index helps SQLite find rows without scanning the full table for some query shapes. Indexes occupy space and make writes more expensive. Examine the plan for the query you actually run.

api.name: CREATE INDEX name ON table(column)
api.description: Maintain a lookup structure for a column.

api.name: EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN SELECT ...
api.description: Inspect SQLite’s high-level execution strategy.

api.name: ANALYZE
api.description: Collect statistics the query planner can use.

lessons.practice: Try a query on title alone. Compare its plan before and after adding a title index.
lessons.pitfall: An index need not be used. The optimizer chooses a plan based on available indexes and the query.
